task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of March 6, 2025. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The Federal Pipeline Safety Commission approved a construction permit on March 6, 2025, for what would be the first dedicated hydrogen pipeline in the United States.
The pipeline, developed by Vantage Green Hydrogen, will run 210 kilometers from a wind-powered electrolysis facility in the Sandover County to a steel manufacturing cluster in the city of Portview.
The pipeline will have a capacity of 85,000 tonnes of hydrogen per year at full operation.

Hydrogen burns without producing carbon dioxide but requires special pipeline materials because hydrogen molecules are small enough to permeate and weaken ordinary steel — a phenomenon called hydrogen embrittlement.
The Vantage pipeline will use seamless austenitic stainless steel tubing rated for high-pressure hydrogen service; the specification exceeds current natural gas pipeline standards.
FPSC chair Sara Osei said: "We developed new inspection and material standards for this permit because existing pipeline regulations were written for natural gas. That work took 26 months."

Vantage CEO Dr. Luis Moreno said: "Hydrogen delivered by pipeline is the only way to decarbonize industrial heat at the scale these steel facilities need. Truck delivery simply cannot match the volumes."

Three pipeline safety advocacy groups participated in the rulemaking and secured requirements for real-time leak detection sensors at one-kilometer intervals and automatic pressure shutoff valves at 5-kilometer intervals.

The Portview steel cluster emits approximately 4.8 million tonnes of carbon dioxide annually from burning coal-derived coke; switching to hydrogen would eliminate an estimated 3.2 million tonnes per year.
Construction is expected to begin in late 2025 and take 28 months; the pipeline would be operational by early 2028.
Vantage has a 15-year supply agreement with Portview Steel Holdings, the cluster's majority owner.

Hydrogen pipelines operate in Europe and in several industrial clusters in the Gulf Coast, but those lines carry hydrogen as a byproduct of chemical processes rather than as a primary energy carrier; this would be the first purpose-built energy-carrier hydrogen pipeline in the U.S.
The electrolysis facility will use 1.4 gigawatts of dedicated wind generation from a Vantage-owned wind farm to produce hydrogen through water splitting.
At full capacity, the steel facilities would replace approximately 40% of their current coal fuel consumption with hydrogen.
The permit requires Vantage to conduct full pressure tests before commissioning and to publish test results publicly.
Five landowners along the right-of-way objected during the permitting process; three have settled easement agreements and two cases remain in negotiation.
The pipeline's operator must complete an emergency response training exercise with local fire departments at least once per year under the permit conditions.
Hydrogen is more flammable than natural gas and burns with an invisible flame, creating unique firefighting hazards that the FPSC's new standards address in emergency response protocols.
Analysts said the permit could unlock similar applications; at least three other project proposals for dedicated hydrogen pipelines are in the pre-application stage.
The permit's environmental review found no significant impacts to protected wetlands or aquifers along the route; three minor reroutes were required to avoid sensitive habitat.
